reasoning: The leaf displays numerous very small (pinpoint-sized), dark brown to black spots scattered uniformly across the surface of an otherwise green leaf. There are no large necrotic lesions, no concentric rings, no powdery or cottony growth, and no leaf distortion. This pattern — tiny dark specks on a still-green leaf — is most consistent with Bacterial Speck of Tomato, which causes 1-2mm dark spots often on foliage. Septoria Leaf Blotch was considered but typically shows tan/gray centers with dark borders and pycnidia.
